title: Defence Money Map — Bundeswehr artillery ammunition and Rheinmetall
scope_note: Public-source investigation into a defence procurement, company economics, ownership and documented lobbying. A contract, lobbying relationship or policy objective does not by itself establish improper influence or causation.

sources.title: Bundestag — Defence budget 2024
sources.exact_location: 2024 defence budget: €51.95bn regular budget plus around €20bn planned from the Bundeswehr special fund for military equipment
supports: The Bundestag described around €72bn of German defence spending for 2024, including €51.95bn in the regular defence budget and around €20bn from the Bundeswehr special fund for military equipment.
sources.does_not_prove: This does not identify the exact budget title, payment schedule or partner-country funding used for each call-off under the Rheinmetall ammunition framework contract.

sources.title: Rheinmetall — 155mm ammunition framework contract
sources.exact_location: Press release dated 20 Jun 2024 · framework ceiling up to €8.5bn gross · initial call-off around €880m · BAAINBw signature
supports: Rheinmetall states that the Bundeswehr expanded an existing 155mm artillery-ammunition framework contract to a gross ceiling of up to €8.5bn.
The contract was signed on 20 June 2024 by the BAAINBw president and Rheinmetall representatives.
Rheinmetall disclosed an initial call-off of around €880m, with deliveries scheduled to begin in 2025.
sources.does_not_prove: The €8.5bn figure is a framework ceiling, not proof that €8.5bn has been paid or will all be called off. This first-party release does not establish the procurement's full competitive record or exact public funding allocation.

sources.title: Bundeswehr — parliamentary approval for major procurements
sources.exact_location: Procurement note explaining that Bundeswehr investments from €25m require prior Bundestag Budget Committee approval
supports: The Bundeswehr states that each Bundeswehr procurement from an investment volume of €25m requires prior approval by the Bundestag Budget Committee.
sources.does_not_prove: This page concerns a different procurement and establishes the general approval rule, not the specific approval file for the €8.5bn artillery-ammunition framework.

sources.title: Rheinmetall — financial figures FY2025
sources.exact_location: FY2025 group figures and Weapon & Ammunition segment
supports: Rheinmetall reported 2025 group sales of €9.935bn and operating result of €1.841bn.
Weapon & Ammunition reported €3.532bn sales and €1.037bn operating result in 2025.
Rheinmetall says the prior-year Weapon & Ammunition nomination was influenced by a significant artillery-ammunition framework agreement.
The company proposed a dividend of €11.50 per share for FY2025.
sources.does_not_prove: These are company-wide and segment-wide figures. They do not show how much revenue, profit or dividend arose from this single ammunition framework contract.

sources.title: Rheinmetall — shareholder structure
supports: Rheinmetall reports 58% institutional investors, 28% private shareholders and 14% other shareholders as at 31 December 2025.
sources.does_not_prove: Aggregate shareholder categories do not identify a single ultimate beneficiary of public procurement spending, nor do they show which investor economically received any particular contract euro.

sources.title: Rheinmetall — voting-rights notifications
sources.authority: Issuer publication of statutory voting-rights notifications
sources.exact_location: Voting-right holdings above 3% · latest displayed notifications through Aug 2026
supports: The issuer page lists BlackRock at 7.33% in a 4 March 2026 notification and other institutions above the statutory reporting threshold.
sources.does_not_prove: A disclosed voting-right percentage is not the same as day-to-day operational control and can change over time; it also does not trace contract proceeds to a specific investor.

sources.title: Rheinmetall AG — Bundestag Lobbyregister
sources.source_type: primary self-disclosure hosted by official authority
sources.exact_location: FY2025 lobbying expenditure, Berlin representation, memberships and activity description
supports: Rheinmetall disclosed €820,001–830,000 of lobbying expenditure for FY2025 and 1.80 FTE.
The register lists Rheinmetall as a member of BDSV and the Wirtschaftsrat der CDU among other organisations.
Rheinmetall states that its Berlin representation maintains direct exchange with government and parliament.
The current entry lists zero concrete legislative projects.
sources.does_not_prove: Lobbying expenditure, memberships or access do not prove that Rheinmetall influenced the ammunition contract, the procurement criteria or any political decision improperly.

sources.title: BDSV — Bundestag Lobbyregister
sources.source_type: primary association self-disclosure hosted by official authority
sources.exact_location: FY2025 expenditure, 472 members, board and nine concrete regulatory projects
supports: BDSV disclosed €1,240,001–1,250,000 of lobbying expenditure for FY2025 and 4.37 FTE.
BDSV reported 472 organisational members as at 1 January 2026.
The register identifies Rheinmetall CEO Armin Papperger as BDSV president/board member.
BDSV describes direct exchanges with Bundestag members, ministries and subordinate authorities.
sources.does_not_prove: The association's size, spending or leadership does not prove that any member dictated BDSV positions or that BDSV caused a procurement award.

sources.title: BDSV regulatory project — defence procurement resilience
supports: BDSV disclosed an objective to improve supply security and supply-chain resilience in military procurement and accelerate defence-related review and approval processes.
The project identifies federal budget and procurement-adjacent laws among the rules to review and contains multiple statements sent to government ministries.
sources.does_not_prove: This advocacy objective is broader than the Rheinmetall ammunition contract. Timing or thematic overlap does not establish that it affected the award, price, framework ceiling or call-offs.
